provenance.source: THIN-SKIN-GUITAR-BUILD-ESTIMATE-1 sprint; all three components are engineering estimates with no owner-confirmation artifact.

notes: Burden ($0.75/hr) is an engineering estimate: ~$1,800 station capital (pump, bag, controller, cauls) over a 5-year life at an assumed 500 occupancy-hours/year = 2,500 hours, giving $0.72/hr, rounded to $0.75. Neither the capital figure nor the utilization assumption is owner-confirmed.

Electricity ($0.03/hr) = 0.75 kW x load_factor 0.30 x $0.12/kWh. Load factor 0.30 reflects a pump that cycles to hold vacuum rather than running continuously; it is an assumption, not a metered duty cycle.
Consumables ($0.60/hr) covers bag, breather mesh, and sealing-tape wear. It deliberately excludes adhesive, which is an estimate material input, so glue is never counted twice.
equipment_hour_rate ($1.38/hr) is a true-cost rate: burden 0.75 + electricity 0.03 + consumables 0.60. It is a COST input, not a billing rate.
Record status is 'draft' because every component is an unconfirmed engineering estimate. Promote to owner_confirmed only when a supporting artifact exists.
connected_load_kw (0.75) mirrors EQUIPMENT-VACUUM-PRESS-V1 connected_load_estimate.total_kw; changing the profile should be reflected here.
This rate is small in absolute terms. That is itself a finding: the cost of the lamination step is dominated by operator touch labor, not by press occupancy.
